name: Zophar
bio: Zophar the Naamathite, one of Job's three friends, traveled with Eliphaz and Bildad to mourn with him and comfort him after disaster struck his family and health, sitting with him in silence for seven days before anyone spoke (Job 2:11-13). His lengthy speeches arguing that Job's suffering must be deserved punishment for sin are told in detail in the chapters ahead. Across two blunt speeches (Job 11, 20), Zophar insisted Job was getting off lightly compared to what his hidden sins truly deserved, and described in vivid detail how the wicked's prosperity always proves short-lived and ends in ruin; unlike the others, he did not speak a third time. Afterward, the LORD rebuked him and his companions for not speaking rightly about God as Job had, and had him offer sacrifices alongside Eliphaz and Bildad while Job prayed for them; the LORD accepted Job's prayer on their behalf (Job 42:7-9).
